_comment: P1 of docs/2026-09-05_control_constraint_design.zh.md: the two command hooks on the control rollout (simple-v3, openap-direct cohort, one seed, KRDU + KSJC), paired with the fresh simple-v3 baseline of control_procedure_20260905 (same manifest, roster, split seed). Hooks act per control segment on the rollout's own state where the on-final gate (membership cone floored at 500 m + path alignment) is on: F_barrier_soft trains through the barrier filter (soft saturation; lateral only), F_barrier_infer applies the hard barrier (hard saturation AND hard gate: a deployed filter has no partially-gated rows) at prediction time to the baseline (the safety-layer classic: no retraining), F_barrier_infer_soft applies the SAME soft hook the trained arm uses to the baseline at prediction time, so F_barrier_soft vs F_barrier_infer_soft isolates the value of training through the hook and F_barrier_infer_soft vs F_barrier_infer the hardness pair alone, R_nominal_residual trains through the L1 + glidepath nominal law with the command as a ±5 deg / ±0.1 residual. Pre-registered readings: corridor-violation rate on truth-established rows should fall on the F/R arms without the vectored-ADE cost the penalty paid (endpoint gain kept, path middle not pushed); the hook epoch record's gated / clamped (saturated) shares are the 'lazy network' diagnostic (clamped > 20 % with bank skill below baseline minus seed noise vetoes an arm; residual saturation > 30 % reads as the nominal law fighting the data); R vs F on flights whose first on-final row is outside the corridor = the design's 'recovery' question (compare_constraint_arms.py's outside@gate / recovered columns). Same claimed_* caveat as the penalty campaign; compare within control campaigns only.
